verdicts.note: Roll calls re-checked in the cached House XML: yea on ESSB 6346 final passage (2026-03-09) and on ESSB 5813, ESSB 5814 and ESHB 2081 (2025). Several independent votes plus campaign statements meet the addendum's bar for +2/high.

S4 and S5 list votes for budgets funding food assistance, K-12, educator pay, special education and childcare, and more resources for high-need districts. That supports +1. The 'no spending-restraint statements' clause in the basis is an absence, not evidence.
Rent-cap vote and campaign plank (pole_b), offset by the E2SHB 1110 supply vote, give +1. Roll calls confirmed.
Single recorded vote (nay on I-2113) and no platform statement, so medium is the ceiling. Not inferred from party.

S3 says she 'leads special initiatives to ... implement climate action' at Ecology, S6 commits to 'meaningful climate action' and opposes the Centralia coal restart, and S7 lists the transmission-authority vote. The score stands. The dossier Background only calls her a 'special assistant' at Ecology, so the basis wording ('leads climate initiatives') goes slightly beyond the dossier text. The coordinator may add the S3 phrase to the dossier.
Two-term House member and committee chair facing a first-time candidate. -1 fits a mid-length tenure.
The E2SHB 1110 yea vote (state middle-housing mandate on cities) is zoning-preemption evidence, the axis's proper scope.
Sponsorship claim (S9), the HB 1321 accomplishment (S3) and explicit statements (S8) support +2/high.
ESSB 5599 yea is confirmed, and S5 states opposition to restrictions on LGBTQ+ students in athletics. That is topic-specific social evidence, not parental-rights evidence.

ESHB 1296 yea on passage and concurrence is confirmed (the same votes as Morgan, who is scored medium). S5's statement about parental-rights debates is vague, but the two recorded votes support high at magnitude 1.
S7 lists the HB 2515 data-center guardrails and SB 6231 tax-break votes, and S6 sets data-center impact goals. These are guardrails, not a ban, so +1.

Checked against S5 ('So much is wrong with this bill. First, it violates the state constitution ... we cannot allow this to stand'). That is pole_a evidence on the axis's headline example. On the other side, S3 would raise property tax on $1M+ homes and condos, S5 says 'I am for taxing the rich' and would expand the car-tab fee statewide, and the pamphlet (S1) describes the millionaires' tax neutrally ('will increase revenue'). The constitutional objection appears on one page, while proposals for new or higher taxes on wealth appear on two, so 0 ('genuinely mixed') is defensible and is not an unknown. The alternative reading, -1 on the strength of the income-tax opposition, was considered and rejected because his own progressive property-tax proposal falls squarely in pole_b's 'tax wealth' description.

Repeated across the pamphlet, the site banner and two pages ('Olympia has a spending issue', 'Stop the spending spree', 'balance the budget, control state spending'), and he questions where the homelessness money went (an audit theme). He also proposes some new spending (a pothole team, bridge inspectors, more K-6 help), but restraint is his stated 'primary focus', so -2/high holds.

Social-worker first response, treatment over prison and help for 'those who are stealing for need' (pole_b) are balanced by fewer limits on police for theft and squatting, and by involuntary facilities for violent offenders (pole_a). Genuinely mixed.
No elected office; 'I am not a politician ... looking to shake up the political world' (S2).

This was the closest call. Three pages carry explicit statements: S4 'I will fight for the rights of ... LGBTQ+, and woman's right to bodily autonomy'; S3 on teaching acceptance and more protection for vulnerable communities; S5 on protecting women's bodily autonomy against Christian nationalism. They cover reproductive rights and LGBTQ+ protections, two of the rubric's pole_b examples, but take no position on sports or gender-affirming care. +2 at medium (statements only, no record) is supportable and consistent with Perez's +2/medium on reproductive statements. These are his own statements, not inferences from party.

S5 says 'No data center will be built in Washington if I am elected' and calls data centers a drain that benefits only tech CEOs. A categorical ban is the far end of the 'data-center limits' description. It is one page with no AI or privacy statements, so medium rather than high is right.
